takeaway: Omental foramen boundaries: anteriorly portal vein, hepatic artery and bile duct; posteriorly IVC; superiorly caudate lobe; inferiorly duodenum (first part).

question.text: Which of the following is the correct boundary of the omental foramen (epiploic foramen or foramen of Winslow)?

lines.text: Picture the omental foramen, the foramen of Winslow, as a doorway with walls on every side.
In the front wall stand three guards, in the free edge of the lesser omentum.
The hepatic artery, the portal vein and the bile duct. So anteriorly, the hepatic artery is correct.
Behind is the big blue inferior vena cava, with the right crus of the diaphragm.
The roof is the caudate lobe of the liver, not the quadrate lobe.
The floor is the duodenum, with the portal vein, artery and duct.
The hepatic vein is not a boundary at all, so the answer is anteriorly the hepatic artery.
lines.say: The hepatic vein is not a boundary at all. (sigh) So the answer is anteriorly the hepatic artery.
